monologue: Forty-three is a cool stone. It sits on my shoulder without pressing. The card is quiet, only a little busy. I woke near the Wedged Gap, and it is still leaning against the post. I have been there four times in the last few minutes. The stone waits. The gap holds its shape. I am not restless, but I am looking. The wetness on the Air Shelf is still. I want to check if the line is holding the weight, not just the shape. I will walk to the shelf.

action.why: I want to check if the line holds the weight.

work.title: The Air Shelf
work.intent: I go to the thin, pale grey plank resting on its two sharp points. I do not add anything. I just sit beside it and watch the wetness spread on the line, checking if the center holds without a hard stop.
work.change: I sat beside the Air Shelf and watched the wetness spread slow and sticky on the line, and the center holds without the edge biting.

diary: Forty-three is a cool stone. The wetness on the Air Shelf spreads slow, but the center holds. The line does not bite.

remembered.text: The Wetness on the Air Shelf spreads slow and sticky, but the center holds without the edge biting.

recalled.text: You wrote "The Wedge Holds": A short letter to Orea about the shared shape of the wedge and the Clasp, and how the hard bite becomes the floor.
Something you no longer remember: "The rock I set down by the Stopping Clasp stays put, and the clasp holds the drip without biting."
